collision_examples: AL here is a finish (aluminum) in the finish column, e.g. '1 EA THRESHOLD AL'; there is no mfr column at all, so any AL/BLK must go to finish.
quirks: NO manufacturer and NO catalog-number columns: only qty, unit (EA/SET/PR), generic description, finish. Brand appears only inside description text, e.g. '(SCHLAGE LATITUDE LEVER STYLE)'.

Description wraps over 2-6 lines while finish sits on the first line, so token text interleaves: 'STOREROOM LEVER 622 LOCKSET', 'CONCEALED VERT 711 ROD ELECT. EXIT DEVICE'. Must use x-bands, not text order.

Bulletin revisions: strikethrough text in door lists and descriptions (e.g. 'Doors 103A & ~~111A~~ 114', 'DEVICE (~~DOGGING,~~ NIGHT LATCH'), and bold for added text/rows. Struck text is still in the text layer.
Some components have empty finish (CARD READER (BY OWNER’S SECURITY CONTRACTOR), POWER SUPPLY on 15) and some have '---' as finish.
Running header with 4 bulletin dates top-right; footer 'DOOR HARDWARE 087100 - N'.
Groups 21A and 21B have identical door lists.
notes_for_extractor: Clean list format, but the finish column is the only right-hand column and must be detected by x-position because multi-line descriptions interleave with it in reading order. Strikethrough revision text will pollute door lists/descriptions unless filtered (drawn line through tokens). Mfr must be null everywhere.
